card: Stops chain verification from falsely reporting database corruption and aborting node startup when check level 3 or 4 encounters missing undo data on pruned nodes or AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstates. Using getblockfrompeer restores a pruned block body without undo records, and snapshot chainstates lack undo data below their base, causing disconnect checks to trigger false corruption errors. The change treats missing undo records as unavailable history, halting verification cleanly rather than failing startup. The issue unblocks pending pruneassumevalid work and was identified during review of pruned txindex.
changed_since_previous: Renamed VerifyDBResult::SKIPPED_MISSING_BLOCKS to SKIPPED_MISSING_DATA across validation and node startup code; core verification logic and test additions remain the same.
evidence: "getblockfrompeer restores a pruned block's body without recreating its undo record. If startup verification reaches that block at level >2, it attempts to disconnect it and reports database corruption, preventing the node from restarting." (PR description)
"With ordinary pruning, reaching the restored block requires a deeper check than the default six blocks. The AssumeUTXO case can occur with the default checks." (PR description)
problem: Fetching a pruned block via getblockfrompeer downloads its block body but not its undo data, and AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstates lack undo records prior to the snapshot base. When startup checks or verifychain run at verification level 3 or higher, the node attempts to disconnect blocks, fails due to missing undo data, falsely logs database corruption, and aborts startup.

risk.why: A mistake in chainstate verification could allow nodes with genuinely corrupted block or coins databases to start up without warning, or could mask invalid historical states.

summary: Stops chainstate verification (CVerifyDB::VerifyDB) early without reporting database corruption when level 3 or higher disconnect checks encounter missing undo data on pruned nodes or AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstates. Missing undo records are treated as unavailable history rather than corruption, returning an incomplete verification status. This allows nodes to restart cleanly and run verifychain after restoring pruned blocks or loading snapshots.
